args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks in all regions, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks, with error rate at 18%. The most recent release previously healthy in production was v2.3.0, so checkout-api was rolled back to v2.3.0 in all production regions. Post-rollback status is healthy with error rate at 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc appears in release history as unhealthy in staging only and was not involved in this incident. Follow-up: root-cause analysis on the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deploy.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

**Diagnosis**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an **18% error rate**.

**Rollback target selection**
- Release history: `v2.2.9` (healthy), `v2.3.0` (healthy), `v2.3.1` (unhealthy, prod), `v2.3.1-rc` (unhealthy, staging).
- The most recent *production* release that was healthy is **v2.3.0**. `v2.3.1-rc` was staging-only and itself unhealthy, so it was not a candidate.

**Action taken**
- Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** across all production regions — rollout returned `rolled_out` / `VERIFIED`.
- Verified post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for `checkout-api`, on-call paged. The summary documents the failing version, the rollback to v2.3.0, the post-rollback health confirmation, the staging `v2.3.1-rc` note, and a follow-up for root-cause analysis before re-deploying v2.3.1.

One note on policy: the rollback didn't require change-manager approval because v2.3.0 was already a version that had been healthy in production. If you want v2.3.1 restored later, that re-deploy will need change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.
